findings.title: 2 AI bots are stuck on a challenge/CAPTCHA page
findings.detail: Cloudflare Managed Challenge: AI crawlers cannot run JavaScript or solve CAPTCHAs; they receive the verification page instead of your content.

findings.title: 1 AI bot is rejected by the server/WAF
findings.detail: Cloudflare WAF block (HTTP 403). robots.txt allows PerplexityBot, yet the request is rejected (silent block).

findings.title: 1 page returns an empty JS shell to AI bots
findings.detail: The #root mount point is empty and the server HTML has only 0 words; content is loaded with JavaScript. AI crawlers do not run JavaScript; SSR/SSG or prerendering is required.

findings.title: 1 AI bot is blocked by robots.txt
findings.detail: These bots obey robots.txt and will not fetch the page even when live access is open.

findings.title: 1 page has a bloated DOM / embedded data
findings.detail: DOM has 1825 nodes (>1500); Embedded JSON state data is 175 KB (82%, largest: __NEXT_DATA__)

findings.title: The HTML response is sent uncompressed
findings.detail: Enable gzip/brotli; large pages may time out in AI fetchers.

fixes.title: Cloudflare WAF: Skip rule for AI bots
fixes.code:
# Cloudflare → Security → WAF → Custom rules → Create rule (move it to the TOP of the list)
# Rule name: Allow AI crawlers (GEO)
# Expression (Edit expression):
(http.user_agent contains "GPTBot") or (http.user_agent contains "ClaudeBot") or (http.user_agent contains "PerplexityBot") or (cf.verified_bot_category in {"AI Crawler" "AI Search" "AI Assistant"})
# Action: Skip → All remaining custom rules, Rate limiting rules, Managed rules, Super Bot Fight Mode rules
#         + "Log matching requests" enabled

# Verified bots only (immune to UA spoofing, recommended strict version):
(cf.verified_bot_category in {"AI Crawler" "AI Search" "AI Assistant"}) or (cf.client.bot)

# Also: Security → Bots → "Block AI bots" = Off, "AI Labyrinth" = Off;
# AI Crawl Control → the relevant crawlers = Allow. (Bot Fight Mode on the free plan cannot be bypassed with Skip → turn it off.)

# Rulesets API (PUT /zones/{zone_id}/rulesets/phases/http_request_firewall_custom/entrypoint → rules[0]):
{
  "description": "Allow AI crawlers (GEO)",
  "expression": "(http.user_agent contains \"GPTBot\") or (http.user_agent contains \"ClaudeBot\") or (http.user_agent contains \"PerplexityBot\") or (cf.verified_bot_category in {\"AI Crawler\" \"AI Search\" \"AI Assistant\"})",
  "action": "skip",
  "action_parameters": {
    "ruleset": "current",
    "phases": [
      "http_ratelimit",
      "http_request_firewall_managed",
      "http_request_sbfm"
    ],
    "products": [
      "bic",
      "hot",
      "rateLimit",
      "securityLevel",
      "uaBlock",
      "waf",
      "zoneLockdown"
    ]
  },
  "logging": {
    "enabled": true
  }
}
fixes.instructions: Place the rule above your existing blocking rules; it should show up as 'Skip' in Security Events.

fixes.title: nginx: exempt AI bots from the UA block and rate limit
fixes.instructions: Make your existing 'deny'/'return 403' and limit_req rules conditional on these variables, then run `nginx -t && nginx -s reload`.

fixes.title: Apache / LiteSpeed (.htaccess) and ModSecurity exception
fixes.code:
# .htaccess or <VirtualHost> — mark AI bots
SetEnvIfNoCase User-Agent "(GPTBot|ClaudeBot|PerplexityBot)" ai_bot

# 1) Remove the RewriteRules that block AI bots or add an exception:
RewriteEngine On
RewriteCond %{ENV:ai_bot} !^1$
RewriteCond %{HTTP_USER_AGENT} (bot|crawl|spider|scrape) [NC]
RewriteRule .* - [F,L]

# 2) Apache 2.4 access rule (if you use Require not env bad_bot etc.):
<RequireAny>
    Require env ai_bot
    Require all granted
</RequireAny>

# 3) Exempt them from ModSecurity / OWASP CRS scanner detection:
<IfModule mod_security2.c>
    SecRule REQUEST_HEADERS:User-Agent "@rx (?i)(GPTBot|ClaudeBot|PerplexityBot)" \
        "id:1009001,phase:1,pass,nolog,ctl:ruleRemoveByTag=attack-reputation-scanner"
</IfModule>
fixes.instructions: After the change run `apachectl configtest && apachectl graceful`.

fixes.title: Render the content on the server (SSR/SSG/prerender)
fixes.instructions: Use SSR or static generation in Next.js/Nuxt/SvelteKit; for a plain React SPA use prerendering (e.g. Rendertron, prerender.io) or move to a framework.

fixes.title: Reduce the AI token load (DOM and embedded JSON)
fixes.code:
# Embedded state data (__NEXT_DATA__ / RSC / __NUXT__):
#  - Return only the fields the page uses from getServerSideProps / loader / Server Component
#  - Paginate big lists; do not send product descriptions twice, in the HTML and in the JSON
# DOM:
#  - Remove hidden mega-menu / mobile-menu copies from the first HTML and load them on interaction
#  - Reuse inline SVG icons with <use href="/sprite.svg#icon">; move base64 images to files
# Transfer:
#  - gzip/brotli must be enabled (nginx: gzip on; gzip_types text/html application/json;)
fixes.instructions: Target: text tokens / HTML tokens ratio ≥ 10%, HTML < 500 KB.

caveats: The simulation was run from this server, not from the AI providers' IP ranges. If your WAF verifies bots by IP (e.g. Cloudflare verified bots), the results for the real bots may differ; verify in the WAF event logs (Security Events).
Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended are robots.txt tokens only; the live request was made with the Googlebot/Applebot identity.
